messages:
maria gomez: paging — alerts for dedicated-pool-eu-2 and ./router are flapping. metrics show active_capacity drop to 0 while queue length stays high. first hit ~2187654321. @tyler @devon can you take?

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-21876 — dedicated pool capacity anomaly. PAGER: oncall-rotation. Severity: P2.

pagerduty-bot: @oncall-rotation paged. Please acknowledge: https://pd.example/INC-21876

oncall-rotation: acknowledged — jumping in, assigning to tyler.

tyler ng: looking. quick glance: router fallback policy churned 3x in last 60s, sending traffic to region-us-west-1 variants which are incompatible (smaller KV cache) — responses timing out.

maria gomez: customers are seeing timeouts and 500s for a subset of models (approx 6% of traffic), support already triaged a few enterprise apps.

devon lee: logs show router emitted metric `variant_healthy_weight` flipping to 0 for eu variants, autoscaler saw low utilization -> terminated some pods; when traffic fell back to eu it got rejected. looks like metric mapping mismatch between router and autoscaler (router reports kernel-level load, autoscaler expects request_count).

anita shah: do we have a runbook step for metric-mapping drift?

tyler ng: not exactly. quick mitigation options: 1) pause fallback policy so router doesn't rehome traffic across regions; 2) temporarily pin routing to eu variants; 3) force autoscaler to use request_count signal. I'll try (1) first.

tyler ng: running: `rwctl policy update fallback --id=fp-eu --enabled=false`

ops-bot: Command executed by tyler ng: rwctl policy update fallback --id=fp-eu --enabled=false — OK

devon lee: after disabling fallback, router stopped moving traffic between regions. queue draining but we still have 200/s queue for dedicated-pool-eu-2. need capacity.

maria gomez: can we spin additional capacity manually? customers are impacted.

tyler ng: yes — provisioning a hot pool in eu: `infractl scale dedicated-pool-eu-2 --replicas +6 --reason "incident INC-21876"`

ops-bot: infractl request queued. estimate 45s for instances to attach.

anita shah: alert: autoscaler reported an update too: `autoscaler: mapping=active_capacity -> node_terminate` at 2187654387. That maps to the wrong metric. looks like a recent config push to autoscaler ruleset 2026-11-09 changed mapping.

devon lee: yeah I see the change in git: `eng-infra/autoscaler/rules.yaml` commit f3b9a7 — mapping overwritten. Rolling it back.

maria gomez: tentative customer impact summary: 6% of generating requests saw 5-30s extra latency; ~0.8% returned 500s. Major clients impacted: Acme, NovaPay (both on eu region pins).

tyler ng: infra hot pool up at 2187654440. queue processing rate jumping, error rate dropping.

ops-bot: infractl: dedicated-pool-eu-2 scaled to +6 replicas — completed.

devon lee: rolling back autoscaler mapping now: `git revert f3b9a7 --no-edit && deploy autoscaler-config`

ops-bot: Deploy started by devon lee: autoscaler-config v2026-11-09-revert.

tyler ng: also re-enabled a stricter health-check on router so we don't misinterpret kernel backpressure as healthy: `routerctl set health-sources --only=request_count,kq_wait`

anita shah: good. once autoscaler mapping is reverted, we should re-enable fallback policy but with a cooldown.

devon lee: autoscaler deploy succeeded at 2187654502. metrics show `active_capacity` now consistent with request_count.

tyler ng: re-enable fallback with cooldown 120s: `rwctl policy update fallback --id=fp-eu --enabled=true --cooldown=120`

ops-bot: Command executed by tyler ng: rwctl policy update fallback --id=fp-eu --enabled=true --cooldown=120 — OK

maria gomez: error rate back to baseline, latency recovered. sending a short update to support and customers.

anita shah: quick post-incident checklist: 
- repo: eng-infra/autoscaler/rules.yaml (reopened PR to add stronger tests) 
- add integration test between router metrics and autoscaler mapping 
- update runbook: fallback-policy cooldown recommended default 120s for cross-region 
- investigate why fallback triggered so quickly (state churn from network jitter?)

tyler ng: I will own the PR to add explicit metric-mapping validation tests and a canary rollout gate.

devon lee: I'll pick up the runbook edits and add a small dashboard showing mapping drift alerts.

maria gomez: handoff to oncall for follow-up: @oncall-rotation you can close this page once you've done the post-incident notes with links to PR and dashboard.

oncall-rotation: acknowledged. I'll file postmortem and include customer impact + timeline.

maria gomez: timeline summary (for postmortem):
- 2187654321 alert created (router fallback churn + capacity drift)
- 2187654330 initial page to oncall
- 2187654350 fallback disabled (tyler)
- 2187654440 hot pool scaled +6 (infra)
- 2187654502 autoscaler mapping reverted (devon)
- 2187654568 fallback re-enabled with cooldown 120s
- 2187654580 incident marked mitigated, monitoring in watch

anita shah: follow-up owners: tyler (policy cooldowns), devon (autoscaler tests), maria (customer comms), anita (runbook).

ops-bot: Incident INC-21876 status -> mitigated. Please proceed with post-incident review and RFCs as needed.

maria gomez: closing notes: root cause appears to be an accidental autoscaler mapping change in rules.yaml combined with an aggressive zero-cooldown fallback policy. Both allowed rapid cross-region routing while autoscaler misinterpreted load, which led to capacity termination and request rejections.

tyler ng: thanks team. I'll keep watch for 2 hours and then hand over to biz-hours oncall.

oncall-rotation: incident closed in channel; moving to postmortem doc: https://wiki.example/incidents/INC-21876
